This could result in increased cost of imports, inflation, and unhedged foreign exchange debts while making exports more competitive. The extent to which exports benefit from rupee depreciation depends on foreign market demand, manufacturing capabilities, and the cost of imported raw materials.”Gadia also identified several possible strategies: intervention aimed at correcting disorderly markets, inflation management, policies that encourage long-term capital inflows and improved corporate hedging. Raising interest rates may be useful when justified by inflation considerations, but it would also slow economic growth.The debate has drawn differing views from policymakers and economists.The International Monetary Fund said India should allow the exchange rate to move as the first line of defence. It is to curb sharp fluctuations while keeping enough reserves to meet India’s import needs, repay external debt and deal with possible future capital outflows.The recent recovery shows that measures to curb dollar demand can help ease pressure on the currency. articles.title: Russian diesel tanker heads to the U.S., the first since Trump’s deal with Putin
articles.summary: A tanker loaded with diesel fuel set sail Friday from Russia for the United States, the first shipment since President Donald Trump agreed a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release more fuel into the global market.
articles.body: A tanker loaded with diesel fuel set sail Friday from Russia for the United States, the first shipment since President Donald Trump agreed a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release more fuel into the global market. Trump eased some sanctions on the Kremlin two weeks ago and has since waived more, reversing years of American policy despite Moscow’s ongoing illegal invasion of Ukraine in an apparent bid to lower prices ahead of the Midterm elections. The ship’s departure for the U.S. was confirmed by the Kremlin. The tanker, a Malta-flagged shipped named “Agioi Fanendes,” left a port in Russia’s Primorsk today, according to MarineTraffic tracking data reviewed by NBC News. The ship listed New York as its destination. Energy Aspects, a market intelligence firm, said that it had confirmed with its industry sources that the ship loaded up 298,000 barrels of diesel in Primorsk. The firm said that currently the ship plans to unload that fuel in New York. It is expected to arrive on Tuesday, November 10. The ship’s expected arrival would put it just after the midterm elections. Trump’s Republican party is on edge for potentially heavy losses in House and Senate seats its candidates are defending, driven in part by blowback from consumers facing soaring energy prices. Trump and his administration have scrambled to try to bring down those prices, which have increased in the wake of supply shocks stemming from the Iran and Russia-Ukraine wars. Trump has taken a number of steps to warm ties with the Kremlin and pressure Kyiv to agree to end the war, drawing outrage from Ukraine and its bipartisan backers in Congress. “I believe there have already been reports from the Ministry of Energy that the first tanker has departed for its destinations and that further shipments will continue on a regular basis,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said early Friday. Crude oil was headed for a third straight weekly gain. Brent, the most important global oil benchmark, traded around $114 per barrel, less than $13 away from its highest point this year. Since the start of the year, the average price of diesel fuel has soared from $3.55 per gallon to $6.32, an unprecedented rise of 78%. Energy Aspect’s analysts said the impact of the cargo’s arrival would likely be “limited.” Diesel’s sky-high price has troubled economists more than the jump in the price of regular gasoline because, “the cost of diesel gets into just about everything,” as KPMG chief economist Diane Swonk told NBC News in an August interview. “Everything from … running a farm … cost of food, but also everything across the economy that’s shipped gets that extra fee tacked onto it,” she said. Currently, U.S. daily diesel demand is about 3.8M barrels per day, meaning that Friday’s shipment would satisfy not even a full day’s worth of usage. “Global distillate markets have tightened sharply,” said Bank of America’s head of global commodities Francisco Blanch in a recent note, adding that it signals “an acute scarcity of refined products.” Diesel is a distillate fuel, produced by refining crude oil. “Geopolitical disruptions are exacerbating that shortage as attacks on shipping around Hormuz make energy flows more difficult and costly, while attacks on Russian refining capacity further restrict product availability,” he wrote. Russia has historically been one of the world’s largest exporters of diesel. In September and for some of October, the Kremlin restricted the export of diesel fuel amid a Ukrainian campaign of attacks on its energy infrastructure. It lifted those export restrictions after Putin’s diesel deal with Trump. Easing sanctions on Russia to open up some previously-blocked diesel supplies was just the latest in a number of policy levers pulled by Trump. In just the last few weeks, the president has also signed an order allowing more widespread use of an off-road variety of diesel. The administration also pressured European allies, particularly Germany and France, to urgently release some of their diesel reserves. The administration has also reportedly pushed for a fresh release of crude and diesel reserves, though the International Energy Agency has rebuffed that request. Experts say that even all together, Trump’s actions will do little to help ease prices which have continued to trend higher. “Policy intervention can provide temporary relief, but there is no silver bullet for diesel,” Blanch wrote.

articles.title: GM Analysts Say Buy the Dip as Stock Eyes Worst Week Since 2025
articles.summary: General Motors Co. stock is set to record its worst week in more than 20 months, but bullish Wall Street analysts are doubling down.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- General Motors Co. stock is set to record its worst week in more than 20 months, but bullish Wall Street analysts are doubling down.

The carmaker's stock has fallen 8% through Thursday's close, putting it on pace for the largest weekly drop since January 2025, and analysts are saying investors should buy the dip.

On Tuesday, the company narrowed the top- and bottom-ends of this year's profit guidance range, and its Chief Executive Officer Mary Barra warned that GM faces "clear external headwinds," sending the stock down 6.8% in the worst session since July 2025.

"The bar was high," said StoneX analyst Mickey Legg. "It's a buying opportunity. Most of what spooked the market is timing rather than earnings power."

StoneX's Legg, who has a buy rating on GM, is not alone in his call. None of the analysts tracked by Bloomberg recommend selling the stock after Wells Fargo dropped coverage of the company amid an analyst departure last month. Still, GM shares are down year-to-date, declining 5.1% as the S&P 500 climbed 12%.

Analysts at BNP Paribas, Evercore ISI, and RBC Capital Markets echoed the call to buy the dip after Tuesday's earnings. BNP's James Picariello reiterated his buy-equivalent rating, citing GM's "severely discounted valuation" and unparalleled execution.

When GM last reported earnings in July, quarterly profit beat and management hiked its outlook. Shares rallied over the next few days to touch a record high.

But the stock has retreated since amid lofty oil and high costs, elevated interest rates, and weak consumer sentiment.

"The market has focused excessively on these near-term headwinds while overlooking the company's improving operating performance, margins, and cash generation." said Ivan Feinseth, chief investment officer at Tigress Financial Partners.

articles.title: Oil prices hold above $110 as traders price in Middle East escalation
articles.summary: Oil prices remained elevated on Friday as traders priced in escalating tensions in the Middle East.
articles.body:
Oil prices edged higher on Friday after Houthi attacks near the Red Sea stoked worries of escalating fighting in the Middle East.

Brent crude ( BZ=F ) futures held at $110 per barrel. The international benchmark was on track for its third consecutive week of gains. Meanwhile, West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) traded near $100 a barrel, on pace to finish the week down roughly 0.5%.

The Red Sea area has seen increased attacks recently, including on Saudi Arabian airports and on an Aramco oil field this week.

Saudi Aramco on Thursday ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran , marking the oil giant's first such evacuation since the Iran war began.

This week, the New York Times reported that the US and Israel have reportedly drawn up plans for renewed attacks on Iran after the midterm elections next month, raising expectations of increased fighting in the region.

The US has ordered nonessential embassy personnel to depart Saudi Arabia after a series of attacks at the country's airports and oil fields .

President Trump has said he will not attack Iran before the midterms and has suggested that fuel prices will fall afterward.

On Friday, the national price of gasoline stood at $4.29 per gallon, roughly $1.22 higher than a year ago. Diesel hovered around $6.31, about $2.68 more than this time last year.

A power outage at a refinery in the Chicago area is expected to send refined fuel prices even higher in the region.

"You're going to see a lot of $5 gas prices in places like Michigan, Ohio, Minnesota, Illinois, and Indiana," Gulf Oil chief energy adviser Tom Kloza told Yahoo Finance on Thursday.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: Times Business Awards- Hyderabad 2026 celebrates real estate excellence, enterprise and innovation
articles.summary: The 12th edition of the Brihaspathi Technologies Ltd presents Times Business Awards – Hyderabad 2026 brought together the city’s business leaders,
articles.body: The 12th edition of the Brihaspathi Technologies Ltd presents Times Business Awards – Hyderabad 2026 brought together the city’s business leaders, entrepreneurs and industry achievers for an evening celebrating excellence, innovation and enterprise. Held on Saturday, September 26, 2026, at Novotel HICC, Hyderabad, the event recognised accomplishments across real estate, retail, education, technology and other emerging sectors, highlighting the businesses and individuals contributing to the city’s economic growth.With Hyderabad continuing to emerge as a prominent destination for real estate investment, commercial development and entrepreneurial activity, the awards reflected the city’s evolving business landscape. From residential and commercial real estate to technology-led enterprises, the evening celebrated organisations and individuals translating vision into execution, creating employment and driving sustainable growth.BRS working president K T Rama Rao, who presided over the event as chief guest, underscored the need for a stronger ecosystem to nurture entrepreneurship and encourage private enterprise. Highlighting the role of businesses in generating employment and expanding economic opportunities, he called for greater government support to enable enterprises to grow and compete in global markets.Rao urged entrepreneurs to move beyond incremental progress and pursue larger ambitions by building globally competitive products and businesses. Emphasising the importance of bold thinking and calculated risk-taking, he remarked that “the ambition has to be large” and encouraged entrepreneurs to “celebrate failure” as an integral part of the innovation and growth journey.The evening also featured a conversation with former Indian cricket captain Mithali Raj, who drew parallels between professional sport and entrepreneurship. She highlighted the importance of resilience, consistency and perseverance in navigating challenges and building a successful career or enterprise. Raj also spoke about the additional barriers faced by women athletes, particularly those from smaller towns and rural areas, stressing the importance of strong support systems in enabling women to pursue ambitious goals.Actor and entrepreneur Naga Chaitanya brought a creative business perspective to the discussions, sharing insights into his entrepreneurial venture in the food and delivery segment. He spoke about identifying a market gap, recognising consumer needs and translating an opportunity into a business proposition. Drawing parallels between cinema and entrepreneurship, he emphasised the importance of continuous learning, adaptability and viewing challenges as opportunities for growth. He also reflected on his professional experiences, including his association with Aamir Khan and his work on Tandav, which pushed him beyond his comfort zone.The interaction, moderated by emcee Sabreena, offered an engaging perspective on Chaitanya’s journey across cinema and entrepreneurship, adding an informal and conversational dimension to the evening.Continuing the focus on enterprise building and innovation, Kodoori Venkatesham, Whole-Time Director of Brihaspati, spoke about the importance of ideas, courage and execution in creating successful businesses. He highlighted the company’s work across education, artificial intelligence, analytics and large-scale projects, emphasising the role of technology and innovative thinking in delivering solutions across sectors.Shylender, Managing Director of Marami Infotech Limited, shared the organisation’s growth journey and its plans to expand its technology solutions into international markets. He outlined the company’s transition towards a software-as-a-service (SaaS)-led business model, with around 80 industry-specific solutions planned for introduction in the near future.Real estate sector takes centre stageThe awards segment formed the centrepiece of the evening, recognising individuals, enterprises and projects for their contributions across diverse business sectors. The real estate fraternity featured prominently, with honours across residential, commercial and allied categories reflecting the breadth of Hyderabad’s property market and its growing development ecosystem.The recognition celebrated achievements across the real estate value chain, bringing attention to established industry players as well as emerging names contributing to the sector’s growth. The awards also underscored the importance of quality, innovation, execution and customer-focused development in an increasingly competitive property market.As Hyderabad’s real estate landscape continues to evolve, driven by demand for housing, commercial spaces and supporting infrastructure, such industry platforms provide an opportunity to acknowledge the developers, businesses and professionals shaping the sector. The awards brought together stakeholders from across the business community, fostering interaction and celebrating accomplishments that contribute to the city’s development trajectory.The formal proceedings transitioned into a lively celebration, with emcee Sabreena keeping the audience engaged through the evening. A live musical performance featuring popular Tollywood and Bollywood numbers added to the atmosphere, giving guests an opportunity to network and celebrate the achievements recognised at the event.Brihaspathi Technologies Ltd was the Presenting Sponsor, Pride Motors was the Luxury Car Partner, and Marami Infotech Limited was the Associate Sponsor.Here’s the list of the awardees:The 12th Times Business Awards – Hyderabad 2026 concluded on a note of optimism, celebrating not only business success but also the ambition, resilience and innovation driving Hyderabad’s economic progress. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) fell 1%, while those for the S&P 500 (^GSPC) dropped 0.4%. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) decreased 0.3% after semiconductors and Big Tech sold off on Thursday.The 10-year Treasury (^TNX) yield held below the 5% threshold as investors flocked to bonds. The AI trade sank on Thursday as concerns over rising financing costs and a potential slowdown in capex weighed on already-battered neocloud stocks like CoreWeave (CRWV).
